title: Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works build spaces that can be measured, imagined, interrupted or withheld.
introduction:
Canaletto makes a square readable through perspective. Dalí gives an impossible sequence equally crisp edges. Precision, therefore, does not by itself establish whether a picture describes a plausible world. This selection follows the different agreements paintings ask the eye to accept: an upward view into an oval, a figure enclosed by branches, a city compressed between tall buildings, or bands of colour without a depicted place.

Religious figures and domestic workers provide closer comparisons. Their surroundings may be crowded with identifying objects or almost entirely removed. Ask what each work makes necessary for understanding its subject, and what it can afford to leave outside. The answer changes from one painting to the next.
visitNote: These are twenty selected collection works, not a promise that all will be on view together. Consult the museum’s collection pages and current visitor information for loans, installations and access to individual rooms.

books.title: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition
books.author: Anne Dayez, Michel Hoog and Charles S. Moffett
books.note: The catalogue offers context for Sisley, Caillebotte and the changing subjects of nineteenth-century painting. Use it alongside the older city views to compare how painters handle public space and everyday movement.

works.title: Dream Caused by the Flight of a Bee around a Pomegranate a Second before Awakening
works.catalogueTitle: Dream Caused by the Flight of a Bee around a Pomegranate a Second before Awakening
works.date: 1947 in the current Thyssen record; c. 1944 in the Dali Foundation catalogue
works.credit: Salvador Dalí. Dream Caused by the Flight of a Bee around a Pomegranate a Second before Awakening. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The fish, leaping tigers and sleeping body are individually described with clarity, yet their sequence cannot occupy ordinary physical space. Dalí makes that mismatch productive: the eye recognises each part before accepting the whole. The long title proposes the dream's cause and impending interruption. It supplies a narrative mechanism without making the impossible bodies any less precisely present.

works.title: A Bend in the River Loing in Summer
works.catalogueTitle: A Turn of the River Loing, Summer
works.credit: A Turn of the River Loing, Summer. WikiArt; Alfred Sisley. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The river's bend carries the view beyond the near bank without revealing everything ahead. Sisley connects that route to trees, grass and changing reflected light. Small figures keep the water's edge at a human scale. The scene's coherence comes from a continuous environment, unlike the separate recognisable elements whose incompatible relations organise Dalí's dream.

works.title: The Apotheosis of Hercules
works.credit: Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo. Apotheosis of Hercules. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/giovanni-domenico-tiepolo/apotheosis-of-hercules-1765
works.description: The oval boundary changes how the crowded assembly has to be arranged. Darker figures and clouds gather towards its edges while a brighter opening offers a direction of ascent. Giandomenico Tiepolo constructs the scene for an upward view. The bodies do not simply fill a convenient shape; their organisation depends on the position from which that shape is conceived.

works.title: Young Knight in a Landscape
works.credit: Vittore Carpaccio. Portrait of a Knight. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The armoured youth stands firmly while plants, animals and a mounted figure keep the surrounding landscape busy. Carpaccio combines the concentrated address of portraiture with details that encourage further interpretation. The sitter's identity and the exact meanings of those details require caution. A convincing reading should begin with their relationships, not with the assumption that every object has one settled translation.

works.title: The Crucifixion
works.credit: Christ on cross. WikiArt; Paolo Uccello. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The cross rises through a low, broad arrangement of mourners and simplified terrain. Uccello makes vertical and horizontal directions unusually clear within a scene of suffering. Angular hills reinforce the separation of bodies. The measured construction does not remove the subject's gravity; it gives the figures stable positions from which their relationship to the central death can be read.

works.title: Christ on the Cross
works.credit: Francisco de Zurbarán. Christ on the Cross. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/francisco-de-zurbaran/christ-on-the-cross-1627
works.description: Zurbarán removes almost all the setting available in Uccello's scene. The pale body and white cloth have to carry attention against near black, with the cross supplying their support. The weight of the isolated figure becomes the principal encounter. Narrative circumstances remain understood through the subject, but they are not separately illustrated around it.

works.title: Easter Morning
works.credit: Easter Morning. WikiArt; Caspar David Friedrich. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Three walkers move away between bare trees under a sky that still holds the moon. Friedrich lets the title's religious association rest on a transition in light, season and movement rather than a depicted miracle. The figures give the path a use without dominating the landscape. Renewal is suggested through a world in change, not announced by a central emblem.

works.title: The Grand Canal from Campo San Vio
works.catalogueTitle: Grand Canal, Looking East from the Campo San Vio
works.credit: Canaletto. Grand Canal, Looking East from the Campo San Vio. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/canaletto/grand-canal-looking-east-from-the-campo-san-vio-1723
works.description: The canal joins near steps, small boats and long palace façades within one intelligible space. Canaletto's angles establish the large structure before the individual movements on the water are followed. Different scales remain compatible: buildings can be imposing without making the boats negligible. Clear intervals let urban life occupy the same view as its architecture.

works.title: The Happy Pierrot
works.credit: Happy Pierrot. WikiArt; Jean-Antoine Watteau. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The costumed company gathers around a musician in a wooded setting rather than on a clearly bounded stage. Watteau leaves the theatrical identities active while allowing pauses and still faces to complicate the title's cheerful promise. The pale costume draws the eye, but recognition of a role does not settle the mood of the person occupying it.

works.title: New York with Moon
works.credit: Georgia O'Keeffe. New York with Moon. WikiArt source label: Georgia O'Keeffe Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/georgia-o-keeffe/new-york-with-moon
works.license: Georgia O'Keeffe Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The buildings constrain the visible sky instead of offering an open prospect of the city. O'Keeffe makes height an experience from below, with the streetlamp and a low red accent establishing nearer points of attention. Hard architectural boundaries meet softer forms overhead. The restricted view gives the picture its pressure; more information about the surrounding streets would change its purpose.

works.title: Our Lady of the Dry Tree
works.catalogueTitle: Our Lady of the Dry Tree
works.credit: Petrus Christus. Our Lady of the Dry Tree. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/petrus-christus/our-lady-of-the-dry-tree
works.description: Bare branches form an enclosure around Mary and the child, with golden letters hanging among them. Petrus Christus joins writing, natural form and sacred presence in a compact image that does not behave like an ordinary landscape. The tree's apparent lifelessness makes the central pair more conspicuous. Its boundary directs devotion before every element's historical significance has been interpreted.

works.title: Piazza San Marco Looking East
works.catalogueTitle: Piazza San Marco Looking East along the Central Line
works.credit: Canaletto. Piazza San Marco Looking East along the Central Line. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/canaletto/piazza-san-marco-looking-east-along-the-central-line
works.description: The arcaded rows lead towards the basilica and make the square's large organisation immediately readable. Small pedestrians then break the paving into separate movements and encounters. Canaletto gives the eye two speeds: a quick grasp of the architectural space and a slower examination of its uses. The people keep the measured view from becoming an unoccupied perspective exercise.

works.title: Saint Catherine of Alexandria
works.credit: Caravaggio. Saint Catherine of Alexandria. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The broken wheel and sword identify Catherine through the instruments of her martyrdom, but Caravaggio shows no execution in progress. Their oblique directions gather around a kneeling woman who looks out directly. The subject is both an observed bodily presence and a set of historical-religious signs. The objects explain her identity without replacing the encounter with her face.

works.title: Black, Red, Black
works.credit: Mark Rothko. Black, Red and Black. WikiArt source label: Mark Rothko Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/mark-rothko/black-red-and-black-1968
works.license: Mark Rothko Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The red band separates dark areas whose boundaries remain soft and uneven. Rothko makes close differences carry a structure that a quick glance may flatten into uniform black. Continued looking can disclose relationships without producing a depicted scene. The painting leaves the viewer's emotional response open; noticing its organisation does not require arriving at one prescribed state of mind.

works.title: The Cook
works.credit: Gabriël Metsu. The Cook. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/gabriel-metsu/the-cook
works.description: Fish, vessels and the white-covered table make preparation materially specific. Metsu keeps the cook's face available within a setting that gives considerable attention to provisions and equipment. The room is organised around use rather than simply plenty. The worker and objects explain one another, so the interior cannot be reduced either to a portrait or to a separate still-life display.

works.title: Landscape at Dusk
works.credit: Vincent van Gogh. Landscape at Dusk. Image credit: Vincent van Gogh. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: A narrow yellow-orange horizon holds the remaining light above rough ground and thin trees. Van Gogh lets the foreground stay uneven and subdued, giving that distant brightness greater consequence. The landscape's structure depends on what the fading day still separates. Strong colour need not occupy a large area to organise the whole view.

works.title: The Toilette
works.credit: The Toilet. WikiArt; François Boucher. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The seated woman and the figure attending to clothing occupy a room dense with fabrics, screens and small objects. Boucher keeps their gestures readable within that abundance. Dressing connects bodies to the decorative materials around them, making the interior useful as well as elaborate. The scene's intimacy is produced through an arrangement of service, space and surfaces.

works.title: The Toilet of Venus
works.credit: Venus at her Toilet. WikiArt; Peter Paul Rubens. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Cupid's mirror introduces a second direction of looking beside the immediate contact between the figures. Rubens keeps the view close, with pale flesh, white fabric and small hands occupying much of it. A mythological subject takes the form of an intimate action. The mirror complicates that intimacy by making an image within the image relevant to the exchange.

works.title: The Virgin and Child
works.credit: Virgin and Child. WikiArt; Rogier van der Weyden. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The elaborate Gothic niche gives the pair a stone-like enclosure, while their coloured clothing and bodies resist becoming mere carved ornament. Rogier van der Weyden joins the appearance of sculpture to painted life. The architecture protects and separates at once. It defines the sacred group's place while keeping its distance from the space occupied by the viewer.

works.title: A Balcony, Boulevard Haussmann
works.credit: Gustave Caillebotte. Balcony, Boulevard Haussmann. Image credit: Gustave Caillebotte. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The viewer stands behind two other observers, sharing a prospect already partly occupied by their bodies and the rail. Caillebotte makes looking at the city an action inside the picture. Trees and neighbouring façades remain available, but access to the street is restricted. The balcony gives the men a position from which to see without joining the activity below.

closingSections.title: Test one pictorial rule
paragraphs: Compare how a clear edge works in Canaletto and Dalí, or how an enclosure works around a sacred figure and a city observer. A shared device can serve different kinds of world. Current display, loans and temporary arrangements should be checked with the museum; the selection is not a fixed route through its rooms.
